Three accounts of the same procedure differ in emphasis but not in what they require.

The steps they agree on, in the order all three give them:

1. State the claim so that it could be false, because a claim that cannot fail cannot be checked, and the whole procedure depends on that first move being made honestly rather than in a form that quietly guarantees its own success.
2. Name the observation that would settle it.
3. Record what was found, including when it was not what was expected.
